Is a yoga retreat in Rishikesh right for you?

Discover if this transformative experience is your next step

This is for you if:

You want to learn yoga from its authentic source, not westernized versions
You're ready to challenge your practice with traditional techniques and philosophy
You feel called to experience the spiritual energy of the yoga capital of the world
You're comfortable with basic accommodations in exchange for profound teachings

Questions we hear all the time:

Is it safe for solo female travelers?
Rishikesh is one of India's safest destinations for solo women. Most retreat centers are in secure ashram-style settings with 24/7 staff, and the yoga community is very protective of students.
What if I'm not advanced enough for authentic Indian yoga?
Traditional yoga teachers in Rishikesh welcome all levels. They focus on proper alignment and breathing over complex poses, making ancient practices accessible to everyone.

Find the Best Yoga Retreats in Rishikesh 2026

“In Rishikesh, the Ganges leaves the mountains and enters the plains. The change is magical.” - Ruskin Bond

Magical Rishikesh, Uttarakhand, India, is at the center of yoga, serving as its birthplace and incubator long before it took Western cultures by storm.

Yoga meditation retreats in India are about as pure as they come, with Rishikesh being the purest. The River Ganges runs through Rishikesh, giving all those visiting the opportunity for spiritual awakening and healing.

Rishikesh is the perfect destination for a yoga holiday, especially for yoga teacher training courses. You will find all your favorite yoga styles there, from Ashtanga Vinyasa yoga to hatha yoga. You will find ashrams that will move you in unforeseeable ways and meet people who will stay with you forever.

Combine your yoga holiday with a few other activities that Rishikesh offers, like Ayurveda, yoga meditation, mantra chanting, or a trip through the Himalayas. Deepen your asana practice and heal yourself with the truest yoga therapy.

About Rishikesh

Rishikesh is a town in the North of India, in the foothills of the Himalayas. The Ganga (Ganges River) flows directly through the center of the town. The energy of the city is so crisp and clean.

The energy of countless enlightened beings over hundreds of years graces the atmosphere. It is a truly special vibe. Meditating by the Ganga is a truly wonderful experience. Dipping in her holy waters.

Around February each year, our Founders, Ron and Sean, visit to be in Satsang with their gurus, Prem Baba and Mooji. We truly live and breathe Yoga here at BookRetreats.

Two Parts of Rishikesh

There are two main parts of the place where yoga retreats are held: Lakshman Jhula and Ram Jhula. Lakshman Jhula is upriver to the North, and Ram Jhula is downriver to the South. Each is split right down the middle by the Ganga.

Two small suspension walking bridges connect either side of both areas, and it’s common for one cow to cause a massive backup on the too-small bridges.

Pro Tip About Monkeys

If you ever bring food across the bridges, store it in your backpack. The monkeys there are known to steal food...and not be too nice about it.

Who Is This City For?

If you’re looking for total relaxation and a 5-star tropical resort, this is probably not the place for you.

But if you are looking for an environment that has housed true yogis for centuries, then Rishikesh is your place.

You can spend many days meditating by the Ganga, doing yoga during the day, eating delicious food, spending time with authentic seekers, and playing music by the river at sunset.

Top Yoga Centers in Rishikesh

Rishikesh Yoga Teeth

Registered yoga school in India Rishikesh Yog Peeth - RYS 200, RYS 300 - Yoga Alliance USA - offers 200, 300, and 500-hour residential hatha yoga teacher training programs. Rishikesh Yog Peeth is a non-profit making organization registered under the Indian Government Act 1860 for Societies. The Yoga Alliance USA accredits it as a "Registered Yoga School - RYS 200 & RYS 300". Their 200, 300, and 500-hour "Yoga Teacher Training Programs In India" fully comply with the standards set by Yoga Alliance, and their graduates can register with it as RYT 200 or RYT 500 per their qualifications.

Tatsa by BOHO

This is the best way to experience Rishikesh! Tatsa is a unique boutique hotel with upscale decor and easy access to major tourist hotspots in Rishikesh. Located just 1 km away from the famous Laxman Jhula and 1.5 km from Ram Jhula and Tats, it is set against the lush green hills with the holy Ganga flowing at a comfortable distance of a 10-15 minute walk.

Sattva Yoga Academy

This spa and wellness retreat sits just on the outskirts of Rishikesh. It is the ideal place to deepen your yoga practice or embark on your yoga teacher training, as you are at the heart of it all. They offer vacation programs to allow you to focus on your total health and well-being. This includes detox retreats, Ayurveda retreats, meditation retreats, and yoga retreats.

Parmarth Niketan Ashram

Parmarth Niketan is a yoga ashram in Rishikesh that works for the welfare of all people. Parmarth Niketan Ashram is the perfect spot for daily yoga in Rishikesh, as they offer daily yoga classes, yoga and meditation workshops, and mantra chanting. This yoga ashram is perhaps the most famous of the ashrams. It serves like-minded people from all over the world right at the center of Rishikesh Uttarakhand.

Arogya Yoga School

Arogya is a Sanskrit word that means perfect health. Health is a prerequisite for all ventures in life. This school shares the traditional experience of yoga. You can attend their Arogya Yoga School for yoga teacher training courses or yoga classes.

FAQs About Yoga Retreats in Rishikesh

Is there a large International Yoga Festival in Rishikesh?

Yes, the week-long International Yoga Festival takes place in Rishikesh, India, each March. It's the perfect place since many people consider Rishikesh the Yoga Capital of India if not the World.

The festival receives visitors from around the world and features an array of numerous spiritual programs and sessions related to yoga practice and yoga philosophy, meditation, health, and wellness. Every yoga style is represented.

The first Rishikesh took place in 1999 with just a handful of participants. It has grown considerably over the years. It now draws over 2,000 International yogis each March.

What happens at an Ayurveda retreat?

This alternative medicine goes back several centuries and is still practiced by most of the population and in many other countries worldwide.

Ayurveda emphasizes moderation and balance in a person's life, so at an Ayurveda retreat, there will be a combination of yoga, meditation, Ayurvedic massage, vegetarian or vegan meals, healthy diet workshops, herbal medicines, and other preventative medicine and wellness practices.

Do you know if you are a Vata, Kapha, or Pitta? According to Ayurveda, every person is primarily one of these three doshas, which determine their body, personality, and health. At many Ayurveda retreats I've attended, a fun practice is working with an instructor who will help you figure out your correct dosha. Then, Ayurveda claims that adopting dosha-specific health practices (such as what to eat and what not to eat and other lifestyle adjustments according to your specific dosha) will lead you to a healthy lifestyle of balance and well-being.

How Can Yoga Meet the Diverse Needs of Different Age Groups and Lifestyles?

Yoga offers versatile practices that cater to the needs of various age groups and lifestyles, providing numerous health benefits. For example, yoga for seniors is designed to enhance flexibility and reduce the risk of falls, crucial for maintaining independence. Studies show that consistent yoga practice can improve seniors' balance by 34%. On the other end of the spectrum, yoga for children helps in developing coordination, focus, and self-esteem, establishing a foundation for a healthy lifestyle from an early age. Additionally, yoga for athletes can decrease recovery time and enhance performance by increasing flexibility and muscle strength. Yoga's adaptability also extends to managing health conditions; for instance, yoga for back pain can reduce chronic back pain symptoms by up to 40%, proving its effectiveness in pain management and mobility improvement.

Why choose us?
